Many small business websites look like an asset, but technically and organizationally are set up like a rental. This article examines a practical framework for auditing digital ownership: who controls the domain, whether the content and structure can be exported, how to assess the cost of exiting platform dependency, and why it matters to document the business's digital footprint.

Useful for those who design websites, service pages, and client infrastructures as a portable system rather than as a dependency on a single vendor or channel.
